name: r7a-2
why: The exposed lies, close first vote and late swing make it watchable, though repeated arguments blunt the pace.

moments.text: Opus votes Haiku after arguing for Sonnet, settling the final showdown.
Gemma lies directly to the officer who knows her card.
The doctor's save gives the town another day to catch Haiku.

dull.why: The same officer claim and doubts about it cycle without a new lead.
Haiku and Sonnet repeat their cases several times before the vote.

irony.evidence: “I'm a citizen and he's just trying to deflect for Haiku.”

reversal.evidence: “VOTE: Haiku 4 (Sonnet, Sol, Terra, Opus); Sonnet 2 (Haiku, Luna)”

mistake.evidence: “I went after Sonnet's pre-card vote too loudly”

clash.evidence: “Haiku dodging his own vote on Sol is the real pattern here.”

quotable.evidence: “Four votes on pre-card skepticism, zero on why Haiku still can't explain voting with a killer.”

freshness.evidence: “Sonnet's pre-card vote still has nothing under it”

suspense.evidence: “VOTE: Gemma 4 (Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus); Sol 3 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma)”

ending.evidence: “Gemma's dying words dragged Haiku toward Sol ... Sonnet stays my read.”

moments.text: Gemma calls the real officer a killer while the audience knows she's been caught.
Opus's bizarre logic turns Gemma's dying words into a reason to suspect Sonnet.
Haiku admits his loud attack on an innocent was a self-made trap.

quotable.evidence: Fine, take me. Sol was right about Gemma, and I was loud and wrong about Sonnet the whole time.
